conversation.text:
**Correct — KaTeX will almost certainly never support `\usepackage{...}`** the way pdfLaTeX/XeLaTeX does.

KaTeX is a **math renderer**, not a TeX engine. It doesn't run `.sty` files or execute TeX macro code. Packages like `amsmath` are written in TeX; KaTeX would need each command reimplemented in JavaScript.

The maintainers have said this directly ([issue #3058](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX/issues/3058)): full package loading is "impossible or at least a very long way away." There's no roadmap to add it.

### What KaTeX does instead

It **built-in emulates** many common packages — especially `amsmath`, `amssymb`, parts of `mathtools`, `bm`, `color`, etc. See the [Package Emulation wiki](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX/wiki/Package-Emulation) and [supported functions list](https://katex.org/docs/supported.html).

So this often works without `\usepackage`:

```latex
\begin{align*}
  \E[X] &= \sum_x x \, \Prob(X = x)
\end{align*}
```

But if a command isn't in KaTeX's supported set, `\usepackage` won't help — you'd define it with `\gdef` / `macros` (what we set up for your site).

### If you need real `\usepackage`

| Option | Use when |
|--------|----------|
| **MathJax** (your regular `post` layout) | Broader TeX coverage than KaTeX, still not full LaTeX |
| **Compile with LaTeX → PDF/image** | You need exact paper compatibility |
| **LaTeXML / LaTeX.js** | Full documents, not inline blog math |

### For your distill posts

The practical model is what you have now:

- **Globals** in `overrides.js` (`\R`, `\E`, …)
- **Per-post** hidden `\gdef` block for anything KaTeX doesn't ship with
- **No `\usepackage`** — check [katex.org/docs/supported.html](https://katex.org/docs/supported.html) first; if a command is missing, add a macro

If you hit a specific missing command from a package (e.g. `\argmin` from `statmath`), I can check whether KaTeX already has it or suggest a one-line `\gdef`.

conversation.text:
**Probably not worth it** for your site — especially for a CTMC post with standard probability notation.

### Why the payoff is small

**MathJax still isn't LaTeX.** It doesn't support `\usepackage{...}` either. You'd gain `tex.macros` in one config file and a few extra TeX packages via MathJax's package loader (`ams`, `boldsymbol`, etc.), but you'd still define custom commands manually — same idea as your hidden `\gdef` block + global macros in `overrides.js`.

**Distill is built around KaTeX.** The template ships with `DMath`, `<d-math>`, and KaTeX auto-render baked into `template.v2.js`. Switching means forking vendored Distill JS, disabling the KaTeX path, and re-wiring typesetting for `d-article`. That's ongoing maintenance, and it diverges from [al-folio upstream](https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio).

**You already load both.** `distill.html` includes MathJax *and* runs KaTeX. Distill math is rendered by KaTeX; MathJax mostly adds weight unless something else triggers it.

### When MathJax might be worth it

| Situation | Verdict |
|-----------|---------|
| CTMC / stochastic posts (`align`, `\mathbb`, `\E`, matrices) | **Stay on KaTeX** — well supported |
| Many unsupported KaTeX commands | Consider MathJax *or* add `\gdef` macros |
| Want one shared `mathjax.html` config everywhere | Nice, but achievable with thin KaTeX globals |
| Need `\usepackage{ tikz }`, custom `.sty`, paper parity | Neither engine — compile LaTeX to PDF/images |

### KaTeX vs MathJax (for your use case)

| | KaTeX (current) | MathJax |
|--|-----------------|---------|
| Speed | Fast | Slower |
| Distill integration | Native | Requires custom fork |
| Macro preamble | `macros` + `\gdef` | `tex.macros` + inline `\newcommand` |
| `\usepackage` | No | No (package loader only for supported bundles) |
| Upstream al-folio | Default | Not default for distill |

### Practical recommendation

**Keep KaTeX for distill.** Your current setup (thin globals in `overrides.js` + hidden per-post `\gdef`) is the right model.

Optional cleanups that help more than a full switch:

1. **Skip MathJax on distill pages** — load it only for `layout: post` to avoid double math stacks.
2. **Expand global KaTeX macros** as notation stabilizes across posts.
3. **Switch a single post to `layout: post`** if it needs heavier math and you want MathJax — only if KaTeX truly blocks you.

If you start hitting specific missing commands (e.g. `\argmin`, a weird arrow, a particular environment), share them — often a one-line `\gdef` is enough and cheaper than migrating the whole distill stack.

<content>- `macros`: `object`. A collection of custom macros.
  - Each macro is a key-value pair where the key is a new command name and the value is the expansion of the macro.
  - Example: `macros: {"\\R": "\\mathbb{R}"}`
  - More precisely, each property of `macros` can have a name that starts with a backslash like `"\\foo"` (defining command `\foo`) or is a single character like `"α"` (defining the equivalent of a TeX active character), and a value that is one of the following:
    - A string with the LaTeX expansion of the macro (which will be recursively expanded when used). The string can invoke (required) arguments via `#1`, `#2`, etc.
    - A function that accepts an instance of `MacroExpander` as first argument and returns the expansion as a string. `MacroExpander` is an internal API and subject to non-backwards compatible changes. See [`src/defineMacro.js`](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX/blob/main/src/defineMacro.js) for its usage.
    - An expansion object matching [an internal `MacroExpansion` specification](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX/blob/main/src/defineMacro.js), which is what results from global `\def` or `\let`. For example, you can simulate the effect of `\let\realint=\int` via `{"\\realint": {tokens: [{text: "\\int", noexpand: true}], numArgs: 0}}`.
  - *This object will be modified* if the LaTeX code defines its own macros via `\gdef` or `\global\let` (or via `\def` or `\newcommand` or `\let` when using `globalGroup`). This enables consecutive calls to KaTeX to share state (in particular, user macro definitions) if you pass in the same `macros` object each time.</content>

<content>## Persistent Macros
...
KaTeX’s [macro documentation](supported.html#gdef) tells the author that `\gdef` will create a macro that persists between KaTeX elements. In order to enable that persistence, you must create one shared `macros` object that you pass into every call to `katex.render` or `katex.renderToString`. (Do not create a fresh `macros` object for each call.)
...
For example, suppose that you have an array `mathElements` of DOM elements that contain math. Then you could write this code:
...
```js
const macros = {};
for (let element of mathElements) {
    katex.render(element.textContent, element, {
        throwOnError: false,
        macros
    };
}
...
Notice that you create the `macros` object outside the loop. If an author uses `\gdef`, KaTeX will insert that macro definition into the `macros` object and since `macros` continues to exist between calls to `katex.render`, `\gdef` macros will persist between `mathElements`.
...
### Security of Persistent Macros
...
Persistent macros can change the behavior of KaTeX (e.g. redefining standard commands), so for security, such a setup should be used only for multiple elements of common trust. For example, you might enable persistent macros within a message posted by a single user (by creating a `macros` object for that message), but you probably should not enable persistent macros across multiple messages posted by multiple users.</content>

...

...

...
Persistent macros can change the behavior of KaTeX (e.g. redefining standard commands), so for security, such a setup should be used only for multiple elements of common trust. MathJax is rendering display math instead of KaTeX. It lacks the `\Prob` macro, causing red text. The `$k$` expression stays unrendered because MathJax does not process `$` delimiters by default. The simplest fix is to stop loading MathJax on Distill pages, since Distill uses KaTeX. The KaTeX macros are already configured in the front matter JSON. An empty `ctmc.bib` file should prevent a 404 error. Kramdown delimiters are already set.

Removing MathJax from the Distill layout is the cleanest fix. Distill KaTeX should handle both `$$` and `$` delimiters once loaded. The question is why `katex.min.js` was not included in the previous dump despite the front matter configuration.

The empty byline suggests the front matter script did not apply. Without it, Distill cannot set katexOptions or run addKatex. The script uses an async attribute, which is unusual for type="text/json" and likely prevents the FrontMatter custom element from reading the script.

The front matter JSON is present in the dump, yet the byline remains empty. This suggests the FrontMatter event either failed to fire or the byline rendered before the data arrived. The Distill code sets katexOptions inside the frontmatter listener.

The `async` attribute on the inline JSON script may be preventing the FrontMatter custom element from reading its content. I will examine how `parseFrontmatter` works in `template.v2.js` to confirm whether the script content is actually available when the listener runs.

The headless timeout caused Distill to initialize too late. MathJax had already rendered the display math, so the byline remained empty. A real browser would allow Distill to load KaTeX and render `$k$` correctly. The plan is to remove MathJax from the Distill layout, keep the KaTeX macros in the front matter JSON, and add a minimal `ctmc.bib` file.

Disabling kramdown's math engine in `_config.yml` would preserve raw `$$` delimiters for Distill to handle natively. The current HTML output shows kramdown's mathjax engine converting them to `\[...\]`.
